Every time I come, the service from the receptionists to the assistants and the veterinarians is excellent; I can only thank them for everything they do for Canuca and for their patience with her parents. Thank you so much! 🙏🙏🙏🙏

The worst experience I've ever had at a veterinary hospital.

If you're looking for a hospital where your pet receives consistent, organized care and continuity between appointments, my experience at AniCura Vasco da Gama was exactly the opposite.

My dog, Côco, just 1 year old, has been treated at this unit since the end of 2025. Over these months she has had numerous consultations, tests, x-rays, ultrasounds, been hospitalized, and undergone successive treatments. Despite all this, the problems persisted without a lasting resolution.

At the end of last year, I sought help because my dog ​​was constantly scratching, especially her ears. Dr. Catarina examined her during that consultation. After looking at her ears, she told me she didn't have much experience in that area and that the problem was probably excess hair in the ear canal, advising me to find a groomer to do ear stripping. It was extremely difficult to find someone who performed this procedure. When I finally succeeded, the groomer explained that Côco practically had no hair to remove and that this wasn't the problem, even teaching me the correct way to clean her ears.

Meanwhile, Côco continued to have gastrointestinal problems and went to the hospital several times. In May, she ended up being hospitalized due to severe gastroenteritis. Even during this period, I kept pointing out that she continued to scratch constantly, but her ears were never truly investigated.

Only in July was she finally diagnosed with otitis. On the 9th, another veterinarian diagnosed a fungal infection. On the 16th, that veterinarian was no longer present, and another veterinarian found that the situation had progressed to a bacterial infection, changing the treatment and increasing the corticosteroid medication.

Days later, Côco began experiencing intense diarrhea, which progressed to blood in the diarrhea, loss of appetite, and lethargy, forcing me to go to the emergency room again. I was seen again by Dr. Catarina, precisely the same doctor who months before had told me that the ear problem was just excessive hair.

During this urgent consultation, I was informed that there was no record of the consultation held on the 16th, nor of the changes made to the treatment. I even had to request the invoice for the consultation to prove that it had actually taken place. This situation left me deeply worried and made me lose confidence in the hospital's organization; in the end, Dr. Catarina said she found it after she had already caused panic.

Furthermore, throughout this entire process, I felt a huge lack of continuity. Practically every consultation was carried out by a different doctor. I never felt there was a consistent clinical plan for my dog. On the contrary, I got the impression that each consultation started practically from scratch.

During her hospitalization in May, Côco returned home with dirty fur full of knots, something I consider unacceptable for an animal that had been hospitalized under hospital care.

After so many months, so many exams, so many x-rays, so many ultrasounds, so many treatments, and thousands of euros spent, my dog ​​continues to have gastrointestinal problems and, in the meantime, has developed otitis media which, in my opinion, could have been identified much earlier.

I acknowledge the professionalism of two doctors who instilled confidence in me throughout this process. Unfortunately, this was not a consistent experience with the rest of the care I received.

Tomorrow Côco will be seen at another veterinary hospital. I sincerely hope that a complete investigation will finally be carried out and that someone will be able to treat the cause of the problems, instead of just controlling the symptoms, because my dog ​​is getting worse and worse.

This review reflects solely my personal experience at AniCura Vasco da Gama.
